# `silk/crypto/blake2b`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Portable BLAKE2b-512 state for the unkeyed 64-byte cryptographic digest of RFC 7693.

## When to use
Use [`Blake2b512`](#Blake2b512) where a format names BLAKE2b with a 64-byte digest, such as prehashed
minisign signatures. Use `silk.crypto.sha2` where a protocol names SHA-2. Use `silk.collections.hash` only for
collection keys. It is not a cryptographic hash.

## Details
The state supports incremental input through `update`, consuming finalization through `finish`,
and one-shot input through `hash`. It uses only inline storage and allocates no memory. The
digest is the little-endian encoding of the final state words, as RFC 7693 specifies.

## Gotchas
Keyed hashing, salts, personalization and digest lengths other than 64 bytes are not supported.
If an update makes the message longer than 2^128 - 1 bytes, the program traps. `finish`
consumes its state, so the program cannot update or finish that state again.

## Examples
### Hash a short message
```silk
import silk.crypto.blake2b {Blake2b512}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let message: [u8; 3] = [97, 98, 99]
  let digest = Blake2b512.hash(&message)
  if digest[0] != 186 || digest[63] != 35 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `Blake2b512` with `import silk.crypto.blake2b { Blake2b512 }`.

## `Blake2b512`

```silk
pub struct Blake2b512
```

An incremental unkeyed BLAKE2b state with a 64-byte digest (RFC 7693).

### When to use

Use it where a format names BLAKE2b with a 64-byte digest, such as prehashed minisign
signatures. Use `silk.crypto.sha2` where a protocol names SHA-2. Use `silk.collections.hash` only for collection
keys. It is not a cryptographic hash.

### Details

Give input in parts with [`Blake2b512.update`](#Blake2b512.impl.update) and get the digest with [`Blake2b512.finish`](#Blake2b512.impl.finish),
or hash one slice with [`Blake2b512.hash`](#Blake2b512.impl.hash). The state uses only inline storage and allocates no
memory. The digest is the little-endian encoding of the final state words.

### Gotchas

Keyed hashing, salts, personalization and digest lengths other than 64 bytes are not supported.
If an update makes the message longer than 2^128 - 1 bytes, the program traps.

<a id="Blake2b512.impl.update"></a>

### Method `update`

```silk
pub fn update(self: &mut Self, bytes: &[u8]) -> ()
```

Adds `bytes` to this state in source order. An empty slice does not change the state.

#### Details
A full block is compressed only when more input follows it, because the final block is
compressed with the finalization flag. It allocates no memory.

#### Gotchas
If an update makes the message longer than 2^128 - 1 bytes, the program traps.

<a id="Blake2b512.impl.finish"></a>

### Method `finish`

```silk
pub fn finish(self: Self) -> [u8; 64]
```

Consumes this state and returns its 64-byte digest.

#### Gotchas

The state is consumed, so the program cannot update or finish it again. Use
[`Blake2b512.hash`](#Blake2b512.impl.hash) for one slice.

<a id="Blake2b512.impl.hash"></a>

### Associated function `hash`

```silk
pub fn hash(bytes: &[u8]) -> [u8; 64]
```

Returns the 64-byte BLAKE2b digest of `bytes`.
